title: Goodbye, goodbye, you were bigger than the whole sky 💔 #Broadway #Bro...
transcript: Well, folks, it finally happened. Understudy slips are officially becoming a thing of the past. If you don't know when you see a show on Broadway and a performer is out, traditionally, you would receive a little white slip in your playbill that tells you at this performance, the role of blank will be played by blank. However, we have now seen our first show move away from these physical slips and instead use a digital slip, putting a QR code in every playbill that the audience member can scan, which will take them to a website and show them who is on for that performance. The site does include options to view past dates, as well as print out your cast list if you really want to. However, while I do agree that this is a more environmentally friendly solution, as a fan, I'm kind of disappointed to see these go. As someone who keeps all of my old playbills and cast lists, I love going back and looking through them and having a memento of seeing a specific performer in a role that not a lot of people got to see. Now, like I said, it does seem like the digital version is keeping a backlog of old dates, although it's unclear how long they're gonna keep them up. Like, in 5 years, are you gonna be able to go back and check yesterday's performance? I don't know. And even if they did, are you gonna remember the Exact date that you saw a show five years ago? Probably not. But this is something that we've known has been coming for a while. It was a part of the most recent production contract agreement between Actors Equity and the Broadway League. And so while for now it seems to be just chess doing it, it does seem like we will be seeing the rest of the shows on Broadway following suit very soon.
